input.content: A React hook is a function that lets you use state and other React features in function components. The useState hook returns a pair: the current state value and a function that updates it. The useEffect hook lets you perform side effects such as data fetching or subscriptions in function components. Hooks must be called at the top level of a function component—never inside loops, conditions, or nested functions. Custom hooks let you extract stateful logic into reusable functions whose names start with 'use'.

input.content: Async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises in JavaScript. The async keyword before a function makes the function return a Promise automatically. The await keyword can only be used inside an async function; it pauses execution until the awaited Promise resolves or rejects. Error handling for async/await uses standard try/catch blocks, just like synchronous code. Promise.all allows you to run multiple async operations in parallel and wait for all of them to finish.

input.content: An index in a relational database is a separate structure that speeds up lookups on one or more columns. A B-tree index stores keys in sorted order, which makes equality and range queries fast. Every index must be updated on insert, update and delete, so indexes trade write throughput for read speed. A composite index over (a, b) can serve queries filtering on a alone, or on a and b together, but not on b alone—the leftmost prefix rule. A covering index contains every column a query needs, letting the database answer from the index without touching the table.

input.content: CSS Flexbox lays out items along a main axis. display: flex turns an element into a flex container. justify-content aligns items along the main axis, and align-items aligns them along the cross axis. flex-direction switches the main axis between row and column.

input.content: Code review works best when the change is small enough to read in one sitting. The author opens a pull request describing what changed and why, not merely what the diff shows. Reviewers look for correctness first, then clarity, then style—style disagreements that a formatter could settle should be automated rather than argued. A review that only says 'looks good' provides no signal; a useful review either asks a question or names something specific. Approving a change makes the reviewer a co-owner of it.

input.content: SQL injection happens when user input is concatenated into a query string, letting an attacker change the query's structure rather than only its values. Parameterised queries stop this by sending the query and its parameters separately, so the database never parses user data as SQL. Escaping input is a weaker defence: it depends on getting every context right, and one missed case is a hole. The principle generalises—injection bugs of every kind come from mixing code and data in one channel.
